entries.name: Michelle Edmison
entries.who: Registered physiotherapist, UBC clinical instructor, and certified Kinstretch and FRC mobility specialist running Movement 101 out of North Vancouver.
entries.why: The biggest fitness-education account in the city — over 75,000 students have gone through her online mobility classes, and her feed turns clinical rehab into training you can actually do.
entries.takeaway: Teach one narrow thing better than anyone and the audience compounds.

entries.name: Meghan Callaway
entries.who: North Vancouver strength coach with 22+ years in the trade and a UBC kinesiology degree.
entries.why: Her Ultimate Pull-Up Program has been run by lifters in 47 countries, and she publishes for Girls Gone Strong and half the industry's major outlets — a global product built from a local coaching practice.
entries.takeaway: Productize your best protocol; a program outscales your calendar.

entries.name: Gary Robbins
entries.who: North Vancouver ultrarunner, HURT 100 course-record holder, and co-founder of the Coast Mountain Trail Series.
entries.why: His three heartbreak near-misses at the Barkley Marathons made him one of the most famous endurance athletes in the country, and he converted that fame into races the whole North Shore runs.
entries.takeaway: A public failure, handled with class, builds more trust than a quiet win.

entries.name: Louise Green
entries.who: North Vancouver trainer, author, and founder of the Big Fit Girl brand and app.
entries.why: A SELF Magazine columnist profiled by People, she has spent nearly two decades building size-inclusive training into a movement, an app, and a book that changed who gyms think they serve.
entries.takeaway: Serve the audience the industry ignores and you own the category.

entries.name: Dr. Jeff Yoo
entries.who: Emergency physician at St. Paul's Hospital, UBC faculty, and elite rock climber.
entries.why: Blends ER medicine with climbing and injury-recovery content few creators can credibly touch — the rare account where the medical authority is real.
entries.takeaway: Pair your credential with your obsession; the overlap is the niche.

entries.name: Desiree Nielsen
entries.who: Vancouver registered dietitian, host of The Allsorts Podcast, and bestselling author of Eat More Plants.
entries.why: One of Canada's most-cited voices on plant-based nutrition, with books, national media, and a clinical practice behind the content.
entries.takeaway: Books and podcasts age better than posts — build assets, not just feeds.

entries.name: Bill Wong — Dr. Swole
entries.who: UBC-trained medical doctor and WNBF Pro natural physique athlete behind the Ask Dr. Swole channel and Swole Radio podcast.
entries.why: Roughly 300,000 YouTube subscribers trust him because he competes drug-free and prescribes like a physician — evidence first, hype never.
entries.takeaway: Skin in the game plus a credential beats either one alone.

entries.name: Lindsay Pleskot
entries.who: Registered dietitian since 2010, formerly running heart-health and diabetes programs at St. Paul's Hospital, now behind a private practice and coaching app.
entries.why: Bestselling author of The Feel-Good Meal Plan who took hospital-grade nutrition counselling and made it feel like talking to a friend.
entries.takeaway: Clinical rigor delivered warmly is a moat — most accounts pick one.

entries.name: Adrian Leung
entries.who: Vancouver online coach who has trained 600+ professional women over six years, ranked among top TikTok fitness voices in 2022 and 2024.
entries.why: Built a coaching brand on one sharp promise: lose weight without giving up your cultural foods — specificity the generic macro coaches can't match.
entries.takeaway: Name the exact person you serve and the exact thing they keep.

entries.name: Reese
entries.who: Certified personal trainer splitting time between Vancouver and San Francisco, with a paid fitness and wellness community and 1:1 online training business.
entries.why: One of the fastest-growing fitness accounts tied to the city — approachable strength content that converts followers into coached clients.
entries.takeaway: Free content is the funnel; the community is the business.

entries.name: Jazmin Gillespie
entries.who: Vancouver certified trainer and international figure competitor with a 3rd-degree black belt in karate, coaching in person at P.R. Fitness Studio and online.
entries.why: The biggest physique following in the city — a mother of two training 5-7 days a week and showing exactly how the shoulders and quads got built.
entries.takeaway: Short, brutal, consistent sessions beat long occasional ones — and film them.

entries.name: Vancouver Dietitians
entries.who: Joint practice and content brand of registered dietitians Alexandra Inman and Stephanie Dang in South Granville.
entries.why: Two clinicians, one account, one message — health gain over weight loss — grown into one of the city's largest nutrition followings.
entries.takeaway: A partnership halves the content load and doubles the credibility.

entries.name: Kellen Wilson
entries.who: IFBB Pro Classic Physique competitor from the Vancouver area — two-time Olympian with four pro wins.
entries.why: Won the 2026 Vancouver Pro on home soil, backed by Mutant Nation and Wolfpak — the city's highest-placed active bodybuilder.
entries.takeaway: Win the hometown title; local proof travels further than reach.

entries.name: Jenn Messina
entries.who: North Vancouver registered dietitian with 15+ years of clinical experience running an intuitive-eating private practice.
entries.why: Built a 45K following on anti-diet, Health at Every Size nutrition — clinical patience in a space full of 30-day promises.
entries.takeaway: Refusing to sell quick fixes is itself a positioning strategy.

entries.name: Phaedra Wright
entries.who: Founder and CEO of VIP Fitness & Lifestyle on West Broadway, running her transformation studio since 2011.
entries.why: A 14-year-old brick-and-mortar coaching business plus a personal account near 175K — proof the studio and the feed can grow each other.
entries.takeaway: The studio gives the content a home; the content fills the studio.

entries.name: Kelsey Ellis
entries.who: Vancouver certified trainer and body-positive fitness voice behind Healthy With Kelsey, known for curvy-girl running content.
entries.why: Carries the weight-inclusive training conversation to a six-figure audience — the running content reaches people the industry told to stay home.
entries.takeaway: Represent the client the ads ignore and they will find you.

entries.name: Niki Mahmoudi
entries.who: West Vancouver online coach and UBC grad building routines-not-trends training for women across Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube.
entries.why: Supplement partnerships and a three-platform presence built on the least glamorous promise in fitness: consistency.
entries.takeaway: Boring promises, kept publicly, out-earn exciting ones broken quietly.

entries.name: Cam Lee
entries.who: Vancouver RYT-200 yoga teacher and aerial yoga specialist creating across Instagram and TikTok.
entries.why: Turned aerial yoga — a niche within a niche — into a six-figure cross-platform audience with consistently inventive movement content.
entries.takeaway: Visual novelty earns the follow; teaching quality earns the stay.

entries.name: Matt Vena
entries.who: Vancouver 93kg powerlifter — junior Canadian national champion with all-time bench press records, equipped 800+ lb and raw 600+ lb.
entries.why: SBD-affiliated and one of the strongest pressers the country has produced, documenting the grind rep by rep.
entries.takeaway: One world-class lift is a stronger brand than ten good ones.

entries.name: Hilary Matheson
entries.who: Squamish ultrarunner, award-winning photographer, co-founder of Here For The Women's Race, and co-host of The Trail Network podcast.
entries.why: Races, shoots, writes, and advocates in the same sport — the connective tissue of BC's trail-running scene.
entries.takeaway: Being the scene's documentarian makes you central to it.

entries.name: Daniela Dib
entries.who: Former SoulCycle instructor in New York and LA who came home to open DibFit Cycle, a boutique cycling studio on Homer Street downtown.
entries.why: Brought big-market spin pedigree back to Vancouver and built the studio around her own name and following — local press covered the opening.
entries.takeaway: Train in the biggest market you can, then bring the standard home.

entries.name: Caroline Doucet
entries.who: Vancouver registered dietitian behind the Nourished by Caroline practice and recipe blog.
entries.why: Non-diet, plant-forward coaching with a recipe library that keeps an audience fed between consults.
entries.takeaway: Recipes are retention; every save is a return visit.

entries.name: Farhad Khan
entries.who: North Vancouver yoga teacher and sound healer who founded Maa Yoga & Wellness in 2007, ran it for 15 years, and now leads sound-healing certifications.
entries.why: The biggest wellness following in the region; his sound-bath and meditation content pulls a global audience into practices Vancouver studios teach every day.
entries.takeaway: Sell the certification, not just the session — teach teachers.

entries.name: Karin Keller
entries.who: Vancouver photographer and creator documenting hiking, skiing, and trail running across the North Shore and Sea-to-Sky corridor.
entries.why: The account that makes Vancouver's outdoor gym — the mountains — look like the best training facility in the country, because it is.
entries.takeaway: Your city's terrain is content no competitor can copy.

entries.name: Deryn Macey
entries.who: Vancouver writer, recipe developer, and photographer behind the Running on Real Food blog, with strength-training programs on the side.
entries.why: A decade-deep vegan recipe archive that ranks in search and feeds a stable audience most algorithm-chasers would envy.
entries.takeaway: SEO content compounds while reels depreciate.

entries.name: Tanvi Parikh
entries.who: Vancouver coach behind I Will Get Lean, focused on fat loss for women with insulin resistance.
entries.why: Took one under-served metabolic problem and built a quarter-million-strong audience around solving it.
entries.takeaway: Pick the problem your audience has been told is their fault, and solve it.

entries.name: Zachary Klassen
entries.who: Vancouver online coach (Project Transform X) focused on women's health — PCOS, thyroid, and menopause — through nutrition and metabolism.
entries.why: Claims 1,000+ client transformations in two years by coaching conditions, not just calories.
entries.takeaway: Specialize in the client the industry finds too complicated.

entries.name: Veronica Skye
entries.who: Founder of Mondays Run Club, started in 2021 with an open Instagram invite to run the seawall and grab a beer.
entries.why: Now 100+ runners show up weekly — one of the largest social run communities in the city, built from a single post.
entries.takeaway: Lower the barrier to entry and the community does the marketing.

entries.name: Clara Roberts-Oss
entries.who: Vancouver Vinyasa teacher since 2006, founder of the Lila School of Vinyasa Yoga and the Practice with Clara online studio.
entries.why: Teaches teachers through her own school, runs a subscription studio, and headlines stages like Wanderlust Whistler — a full yoga business built on two decades of practice.
entries.takeaway: A school and a subscription outlast any studio schedule.

entries.name: Shawn Adair
entries.who: Founder and president of The Bar Strength & Conditioning in Richmond — manual therapist stacked with FST, FRC, DNS, and PPSC certifications.
entries.why: The prehab-rehab coach other Vancouver trainers follow to fix what their programs break.
entries.takeaway: Be the practitioner practitioners refer to.

entries.name: Lucy Ulmer
entries.who: Co-founder of Spin Society and Hustle studios, creator of The LU Method for prenatal, postpartum, and pelvic-floor training — profiled by The Globe and Mail.
entries.why: Built two of the city's known boutique studios, then built the specialized program the boutique market wasn't serving.
entries.takeaway: Your second act should serve the clients your first act created.

entries.name: Abtin Javidi
entries.who: Vancouver bodybuilding prep coach — Body Classic champion with an MBA and ISSA and DotFit certifications.
entries.why: Runs a stage-prep coaching business where the before-and-afters are his own competitors.
entries.takeaway: Client results on a stage are testimonials with judges.

entries.name: Sydney Hara
entries.who: Founded Slow Girls Run Club in 2023 — a no-pressure running community for women in Vancouver.
entries.why: Named the pace in the club name and removed the single biggest reason women skip run clubs: fear of being last.
entries.takeaway: Say the quiet objection out loud in your brand name.

entries.name: Ashley Wiles
entries.who: Founder and head coach of Sole Girls — a running and self-esteem program for girls with 14 locations, expanded to Australia — and a two-time Ironman.
entries.why: Named most inspiring coach in North America by Brooks; the follower count wildly understates the footprint.
entries.takeaway: Impact scales through programs, not posts.

entries.name: Sapphire Amegago
entries.who: Vancouver fitness creator documenting the training life that followed a 60-pound weight loss.
entries.why: One of the city's largest fitness audiences, built on the most relatable arc in the gym: the journey, not the destination.
entries.takeaway: Document the journey in public; the audience arrives mid-story.

entries.name: Andie
entries.who: Vancouver Registered Holistic Nutritionist blending food, fitness, and lifestyle content.
entries.why: A top-three name on BC fitness-influencer roundups for making sustainable habits look livable, not punishing.
entries.takeaway: Sell the lifestyle people can keep on a Tuesday in November.

entries.name: Kyle Vis
entries.who: HYROX Canada L1 coach and Pacific Northwest regional manager, 20-time HYROX finisher coaching hybrid athletes out of Vancouver.
entries.why: The official face of the fastest-growing fitness race format in the region — small following, outsized gatekeeper role.
entries.takeaway: Get institutional the moment a new sport arrives in your city.

entries.name: Arisha Ladhani
entries.who: Vancouver-raised athlete and creator behind Wake Up and Kale, splitting time between Vancouver and LA.
entries.why: Healthy-recipe and balanced-lifestyle content with CTV Morning Live appearances — a mainstream bridge into fitness culture.
entries.takeaway: Morning-TV friendliness is a distribution channel most lifters ignore.

entries.name: Jack Craddock
entries.who: Vancouver Classic Physique competitor who earned his IFBB Pro Card at the July 2026 Vancouver Pro.
entries.why: Went from local CPA shows to the pro stage in three seasons, placing 4th in his pro debut at home.
entries.takeaway: Momentum is a story people follow in real time — narrate the climb.

entries.name: Fiona Stang
entries.who: Authorized Ashtanga teacher leading Ashtanga Yoga Vancouver, one of the city's traditional practice communities.
entries.why: Authorization in the Ashtanga lineage is rare currency — a decades-deep practice, not a 200-hour certificate.
entries.takeaway: Lineage and rarity beat reach in trust-driven disciplines.

entries.name: Kianoosh Azar
entries.who: Vancouver-based ISSA online trainer — national bodybuilding champion, 2nd at the IFBB Diamond Cup, 4th on the amateur Olympia circuit.
entries.why: An international competition résumé compressed into an online coaching practice.
entries.takeaway: Compete internationally, coach locally, sell globally.

entries.name: Sharan Scali
entries.who: Owner of Semiahmoo Athletic Club in South Surrey — competitive Olympic weightlifter, CrossFit coach, and nutrition specialist.
entries.why: Competes in the sports she coaches and owns the floor she coaches on — full-stack credibility under one roof.
entries.takeaway: Own the gym, lift the meets, coach the members — the loop sells itself.

entries.name: Ana
entries.who: E-RYT 500 yoga teacher and yoga therapist, faculty on a Vancouver-area teacher training program.
entries.why: Trains the city's next generation of teachers — upstream of every studio schedule.
entries.takeaway: Teacher trainers sit upstream of the whole local market.

entries.name: Emily Adams
entries.who: Vancouver-based certified trainer and contest-prep coach (Team Mutant, Better Bodies) training clients out of Port Coquitlam.
entries.why: Combines a women's online coaching business with BC outdoor-lifestyle content that doesn't feel like an ad.
entries.takeaway: Sponsors follow athletes who already look sponsored.

entries.name: Wyatt Hunter
entries.who: Team Canada weightlifter, 2023 Commonwealth champion at 89kg, UBC kinesiology student and Dynasty Weightlifting coach.
entries.why: Training for LA 2028 out of a downtown Vancouver gym while running the UBC Weightlifting Club — the city's Olympic hope in the sport.
entries.takeaway: Document the road to the Games before the Games make it crowded.

entries.name: Abby Verigin
entries.who: Burnaby yoga therapist (C-IAYT track) and group fitness coach teaching at Oxygen Yoga & Fitness.
entries.why: A BC top-10 roundup name bridging therapeutic yoga and group fitness floors.
entries.takeaway: Therapeutic depth differentiates a group-fitness résumé.

entries.name: Gracie
entries.who: Vancouver fitness creator whose gym-humor and relatable training content built an 84K TikTok following, with KEEPTHATPUMP, Magnum Nutraceuticals, and FitnessAI sponsorships.
entries.why: Proof the next wave of local fitness influence is being built on TikTok, not Instagram.
entries.takeaway: Humor lowers the barrier to the gym better than another form-check reel.

entries.name: Taylor Logan
entries.who: Vancouver yoga teacher and blogger behind the Yogini Taylor class business, writing on yoga, motherhood, and mindfulness.
entries.why: A personal-brand yoga business — classes, blog, and audience — run end to end by one teacher.
entries.takeaway: Own your booking page; don't rent your students from a studio.

entries.name: Sandra Kilmartin
entries.who: Sports dietitian with the IOC Diploma in Sports Nutrition, ultrarunner, and founder of No Sweat Nutrition serving Vancouver and the Sea to Sky.
entries.why: The fueling expert behind local endurance athletes — Olympic-committee-credentialed in a field crowded with certificates.
entries.takeaway: The smallest audiences can hold the highest-value clients.

entries.name: SarahB Fit
entries.who: Vancouver bikini competitor and long-running fitness creator.
entries.why: A fixture of the local competition scene since the Daily Hive was rounding up fitness Instagrammers in 2017.
entries.takeaway: Longevity in a churn industry is its own credential.
